country.comment: Primary ethnographic site is the Quang Trung social housing complex in Vinh City, Nghệ An Province, Vietnam; supplemental interviews with East German technicians and archival research were also conducted in Germany (Berlin) and Hanoi regarding Vinh's reconstruction.
country.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract and main text; PDF p. 3; PDF p. 14, Note 1

effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative ethnographic and historical analysis; descriptive physical/budgetary figures (e.g., 19 blocks, >8,000 original state employees, 700 million VND / ~US$35,000 biennial maintenance budget, household monthly water bills of 30,000–55,000 VND, communal repair fee of 100,000 VND) are contextual rather than statistical effect estimates.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. State point-and-rank housing allocation privileged higher-ranking cadres and officials with lower-floor apartments (first and second floors) where water pressure reached, while workers and lower-level civil servants on floors 3–5 faced dry taps, nightly water hauling between 11:00 p.m. and 2:00 a.m., and clogged wastewater drains for nearly two decades; following 1986 Đổi mới reforms and unit privatization, ambiguous ownership/tenure and underfunded municipal management (Division of Housing budget of 700 million VND / ~US$35,000 every two years for 19 blocks) produced contested repair liability, chronic pipe and toilet leaks, structural water damage, and resident resistance to state-shifted maintenance costs.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 9–13; PDF p. 14, Notes 2, 3, 14, and 22

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by qualitative study design (CASP Qualitative Checklist). Rated 2 because the author directly observed and documented administrative, property/liability, allocation, and fee mechanisms operating on household water and sanitation conditions through 9 months of residential participant observation, interviews with residents and the managing housing official, and archival records.
mechanism_certainty.where_found: PDF pp. 2–3; PDF pp. 9–13; PDF p. 14, Notes 1–3, 14, and 22

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines socialist modernist urban/housing planning and bureaucratic rank/point-based apartment allocation (planning, property, tenure), post-Đổi mới privatization creating ambiguous ownership and contested repair liability between the municipal Division of Housing and tenant-owners (property, tenure, institutional_fragmentation), mandatory communal repair fees and utility charges (fees), and public press petitions/complaints to the water company and housing authorities (complaint).
mechanism_flags.value: ELIGIBILITY, BURDEN, ENFORCEMENT, property, tenure, planning, fees, complaint, institutional_fragmentation
mechanism_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 2–4; PDF pp. 9–13; PDF pp. 14–15, Notes 3, 14, 22, and 23

outcome_flags.comment: Documents dry indoor taps and reliance on public spouts/wells (water_access), indoor squat toilets and clogged/overflowing wastewater drains (sanitation_access), low hydraulic pressure, chronic leaks, and breakdown (service_reliability), intermittent brief nightly water delivery between 11:00 p.m. and 2:00 a.m. (service_continuity), and unfiltered murky water and sewage odors/mold (service_quality).
outcome_flags.where_found: PDF pp. 2–3; PDF pp. 9–13; PDF p. 14, Note 21

sample_size.value: 1 social housing complex (Quang Trung, 19 remaining housing blocks; exact number of interviewees not reported)
